passage: Confidential note from Madhuri, member of the workplace committee. Vandana came to see me on Tuesday, unsure whether what she had experienced was "serious enough." She said a senior colleague had been commenting on her appearance, and once put a hand on her shoulder after she had told him to stop. She had not reported it because she doubted herself. I told her it is serious, that it is not her fault, and that she did not need a name for it to be allowed to speak. Together we wrote down the dates and what was said. She then told the colleague, in writing, that the comments must stop. I explained the committee's steps, and she chose to file a formal complaint that same day. I checked in with her on Thursday and again a week later.

qa.q: What did Vandana tell the colleague in writing?
qa.a: She told him that the comments must stop.

qa.q: Why had Vandana not reported it earlier?
qa.a: She doubted herself and wondered whether it was serious enough.

qa.q: What did Madhuri do after listening to Vandana?
qa.a: Madhuri said it was serious and not her fault, wrote down the dates and words with her, explained the committee's steps and checked in later.

qa.q: How might Vandana have felt on hearing that it was serious?
qa.a: She may have felt relieved to be believed, though possibly still nervous about filing.

grounding: A committee member's note shows a colleague's unwanted remarks and touch being taken seriously, with a clear no, written details and use of the committee.

passage:
It started small. Rakesh from accounts would lean on the back of my chair and say my kurtas were "distracting today". Then his hand on my shoulder, staying a second too long. I'm Yamini, I'd been at the firm eight months, and I kept telling myself it was just his way. Everyone laughed at his jokes.
Looking back, what changed things was a Tuesday when he did it in the lift. I heard my own voice say, "Don't touch me. I mean it." He called me touchy.
That night I opened a note on my phone and wrote down every date I could remember, what he said, who was nearby. Next morning I showed it to Uma, the senior manager I trust most. She didn't ask if I was sure. She said, "This isn't your fault," and walked me to the Internal Committee office herself.

qa.q: Where was Yamini when she said, "Don't touch me. I mean it"?
Why did Yamini keep saying it was just Rakesh's way?
qa.a: Yamini felt unsure and uncomfortable, doubting whether it was serious because everyone laughed at his jokes and it started small.

qa.q: Which steps helped Yamini act on the harassment?
qa.a: Saying a clear no, writing down dates, words and who was nearby, and going to Uma, a trusted senior, who took Yamini to the Internal Committee.

qa.q: How might Uma see Yamini's note when it is shown to her?
qa.a: Uma treats it as serious straight away; she seems concerned and protective, which is why she says it is not Yamini's fault and walks Yamini to the committee.

grounding: A colleague's remarks and touch make the protagonist uncomfortable; the protagonist says no, records details, and goes to a trusted senior and the committee.

passage:
Supervisor's note, site office, 14 March.
Pankaj, junior site engineer, asked to speak privately after lunch. He was quiet and kept his helmet on his lap. He said Vivek, a senior on the same shift, has been making crude jokes about his body in front of the crew and last week pinched his neck while he was on a ladder. Pankaj said, "It's probably just how guys joke, sir." Then he asked if he was overreacting.
I told him it is serious and it is not his fault. I asked if he had told Vivek to stop; he said yes, once, and was laughed at. I suggested he write down dates, words and witnesses, and we started the list together. With his agreement I emailed the Internal Committee at 3 p.m. today and moved him to the other shift for now.
Follow-up with Pankaj on Monday.
Aparna

qa.q: What did Vivek do while Pankaj was on a ladder?
How can you tell Pankaj felt unsure whether it was serious?
qa.a: He felt unsure and embarrassed, calling it "how guys joke" and asking if he was overreacting, while keeping his helmet on his lap.

qa.q: What did the supervisor do the same day?
qa.a: The supervisor said it was serious and not his fault, helped him start a list of dates and witnesses, emailed the Internal Committee at 3 p.m., and moved him to another shift.

qa.q: How might the crew's laughter have affected Pankaj?
qa.a: It likely left Pankaj feeling small and alone, as if objecting would make him look weak, which is why an outside, clear response mattered.

grounding: A colleague's crude remarks and contact leave the protagonist doubting himself; a supervisor confirms it is serious, helps record details and involves the committee.
